why_this_file_exists: An R-35 verifier named behaviour no commit body mentions: 69e7323 made ReceiptLedger build and drive an OutcomeLedger for every receipt walk -- that is, for every /api/calculate, /api/bis and /api/optimize request -- and OutcomeLedger's write-once discipline raises. The bodies of that slice describe the ledger as 'refusing a second answer to one question', which is the design and is right. What none of them states is the operational consequence: a condition that previously resolved silently, because the event dict simply took the last write, is now an unhandled exception on a user request. The campaign's own thesis is that a failure must be named rather than anonymous, and 'we joined a raising record to all three serving paths' is a sentence somebody owed a reader. It is written here, dated, with the raise set enumerated from source and a gate that asserts the consequence rather than describing it. -- CLOSED 2026-08-14 by the umbrella's Amendment G: the raise set is bounded on the serving path in the first of the two ways how_an_entry_closes names, a named 500 carrying a receipt, and the entry is retired here with its gate inverted rather than deleted.
how_an_entry_closes: An entry moves to retired[] only when the raise set is bounded on the serving path -- either because the campaign rules these raises into the D-25 boundary shape (a named 500 carrying a receipt, the way ProjectionStarvation is handled) or because every reachable raise is proven impossible over an enumerated roster population rather than over the committed corpus alone. Deleting the entry is not closing it, and neither is widening a catch: an absorbed OutcomeRewritten is the last-write-wins the join replaced.

retired.raised_by: an R-35 verifier on slice group campaign-close, under 'behaviour the commit bodies do not mention'
retired.what: src/calculator/survival/receipt_state.py:412 constructs an OutcomeLedger inside every ReceiptLedger, so the receipt walk drives it on every request. Three of its methods raise: write() raises OutcomeRewritten on a second write to one outcome field, _claim_applied() raises DuplicateApplied on a second APPLIED claim for one (source_key, subject, event_slot), and skip() raises OutcomeRewritten on a second un-preserved skip. Before 69e7323 all three were fixture-only.
retired.why_it_matters: src/app.py wraps every registered view in exactly one catch, _within_starvation_boundary, and that catch names ProjectionStarvation alone (D-25: exactly one catch, allowlisted by a source assertion). OutcomeRewritten and DuplicateApplied are RuntimeError subclasses and are not caught anywhere on the serving path, so a request that trips one returns a bare 500 with no disposition, no receipt and no named field -- an unnamed failure, which is the shape the STARVED boundary exists to avoid.
retired.why_it_is_filed_rather_than_fixed: Both available fixes are rulings rather than lane edits. Widening the boundary to catch these is a second member of the single-catch rule D-25 states, and a lane may not extend that rule. Absorbing them instead of raising would restore the last-write-wins the join was landed to replace, which is the campaign's own failure shape. What a lane may do is measure the reachable set and say so, which is this entry.

retired.for_the_owner: Two questions, both above a lane. Does D-25's 'exactly one catch' rule name ProjectionStarvation specifically, or the class of programming errors a projection or a ledger raises on a request? And if the second, does the STARVED disposition cover a rewritten outcome, or does the invariant table owe a fifth spelling? Until one of those is answered the raise stands, uncaught and now recorded.

what_closed_and_when.by: the remediation lane for slice group campaign-close, on the ruling this entry's for_the_owner asked for
what_closed_and_when.the_ruling: The umbrella's Amendment G of 2026-08-14 answers both questions this entry put to the owner. D-25's 'exactly one catch' is a rule about WHERE a named refusal becomes a response and never a count of the exception types that one handler names; and the disposition is STARVED, so the invariant table owes no fifth spelling -- a record holding two answers to one question cannot answer it, and a leaf with no value a rule computed is the whole of what the word means.
what_closed_and_when.the_change: trigger_stream.StarvedSignal is the class, ProjectionStarvation is a member, and the three ledger raises join it carrying field, producer and reason. src/app.py's one handler converts the base. The source assertion that allowlists exactly one handler and forbids every other is unchanged in force and now ranges over the class, so a member added later is converted rather than newly anonymous.
what_closed_and_when.what_was_not_done: No raise was absorbed and no second catch was added. An absorbed OutcomeRewritten is the last-write-wins the join replaced, and this entry's own how_an_entry_closes says so; the write-once discipline is exactly as strict as it was, and what changed is only that the refusal arrives at a reader with a name.
what_closed_and_when.gate_inversion: test_the_request_boundary_names_these_raises replaces test_the_request_boundary_does_not_name_these_raises and asserts the receipted 500 -- status, the STARVED disposition, and the field/producer/reason the response carries.
